mainTopic: Limiting a big eater or splitting a חבורה, and money received for a share in a קרבן
overview: The משנה rules that if a member of a פסח group adds an outsider to his own share, the group may give him just his portion, and he eats it with the outsider. The גמרא asks whether a group may tell a member with 'fine hands' (a big eater) to take his share and leave. Two proofs, from our משנה and from the משנה about the שמש by the oven, are each rejected. A ברייתא then rules clearly that the group may limit him, even at an ordinary friendly meal (סיבולת). A second version (איכא דאמרי) reads the same ברייתא to teach that a חבורה may split up only for a real reason. A story follows: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע pressed רב פפא with these sources until רב פפא divided the bread, and later רב הונא joked about eating with רבינא. Finally, a ברייתא teaches that money taken for a share in a פסח or חגיגה is חולין, while selling an עולה or שלמים is void and the money goes to נדבה as a קנס. עולא then asks how the money's holiness can pass onto a lamb that is already הקדש.

steps.title: The משנה: adding another person into your share
steps.stepSummary: If a member of a פסח group adds another person into his own portion, the group may give him just his own share. He and the person he added eat from that share, and the group eats from theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone registers another person with him in his portion, the group members may give him his own share. He eats from his share, and they eat from theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a rule about a member of a פסח group who adds an extra person into his own share without asking the group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The group never agreed to the new person. So they may separate out the member's share and let the two of them eat it alone, apart from the group. Everyone else keeps eating their own portions together.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה being studied
One who registers or includes someone in a קרבן
His portion or share
The members of the group that share one קרבן פסח
They are permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule becomes the source the גמרא tries to use to answer the next question.

phrases.english: Mishnah:

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A member who adds an outsider to his share can be given only his own share, which he eats with the outsider, apart from the group.

steps.title: Can a group send away a member who grabs too much food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a group may tell a member with 'fine hands' (who grabs a lot) to take his share and leave. Maybe he can say 'you accepted me.' Or maybe they can say they accepted him only to help finish the offering, not so he would eat more than them.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: If one member of a group has 'fine hands' (he grabs a lot of food), may they tell him, 'Take your share and leave'? Do we say he can answer them, 'But you accepted me'? Or perhaps they can say to him, 'When we accepted you, it was to help with the offering. We did not accept you so that you would eat more than us.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an איבעיא, a real open question: may a group limit a member who eats much more than everyone else?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two sides. The big eater can argue that the group took him in with no conditions. The group can argue that they took him in only so the קרבן would be fully eaten (תיקוני זביחה), and never agreed to let him eat more than his fair share.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
A question was asked before them (an open question)
'Fine hands', a polite way of saying he grabs a lot of food
But you accepted me
For the proper completion of the offering, so that it is fully eaten
More

steps.confusionAlert: 'יָדָיו יָפוֹת' does not mean he has nice hands or is skilled. It is a polite way of saying he is a big eater who grabs food quickly.

steps.title: Trying to prove the answer from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings our משנה as a proof. The man who added others is really eating more than one share, which is like 'fine hands.' Since the group may limit him, a big eater must also be limitable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who registers others with him in his portion: the group members may give him his own share. He eats his, and they eat theirs. What is the reason? Is it not because this is like the case of one member with 'fine hands'? And if you thought a person with 'fine hands' can say to them 'you accepted me,' then this person should be treated the same as one with 'fine hands'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question using the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding people to your share means more total eating on your side, which looks just like a member with ידיו יפות. If a big eater could claim 'you accepted me,' then this man should be able to make the same claim and keep his place. But the משנה lets the group separate him, so a big eater should also be limitable.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, which introduces a proof
What is the reason?
Is it not because…
And if it would enter your mind (if you were to think)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who registers others with him in his portion —
the members of the group are permitted
to give him his own portion,
and he eats his,
and they eat theirs.
What is the reason?
Is it not because it is

phrases.notes: He and his guests together eat more than one share.

phrases.english: And if you were to think that

phrases.aramaic: יָדָיו יָפוֹת מָצֵי אֲמַר לְהוּ קַבֵּילְתּוּן,
phrases.english: one with 'fine hands' can tell them, 'You accepted me,'

phrases.notes: Then he too could not be sent away. Since the משנה says he can be, a big eater can also be limited.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to resolve the question of step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That a group may limit a member with ידיו יפות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה, where a member who added others may be given only his own share.

steps.title: Rejecting the proof: adding a new person is different
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Adding new people (דעות) is a separate issue. Even if the member and his guest ate only one share between them, the group can object to having a stranger among them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: No. Adding new people is different. Even if the two of them together eat only as much as one group member, the group can still say to him, 'We are not comfortable having a stranger among us.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's reason may have nothing to do with eating too much. The group may object simply to an unfamiliar person joining them, even if no extra food is eaten. So the משנה teaches nothing about the big eater, and the גמרא looks for another source (step 7 settles it).

keyTerms.meaning: They say, which introduces a rejection or answer
Separate people (minds) are different
It is not pleasant or acceptable to us
A stranger, an unfamiliar person

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה lets a group separate someone who added an outsider because they may refuse a stranger, not necessarily because of extra eating. So this משנה cannot prove the law about ידיו יפות. A direct source in step 7 settles it.

phrases.english: They say: No,
additional people are different,
for even if both of them
eat only as much as one member of the group,
they can say to him:
'It is not pleasant for us'
'to have a stranger among us.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה. It does not decide the question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה's reason was extra eating, but the reason may be the group's right to refuse a stranger.

steps.title: Proof from the waiter who ate by the oven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: a שמש who ate a כזית of the פסח next to the oven must stay there, and the group joins him only if they want to. So 'you accepted me' cannot force them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a waiter who ate an olive-size piece of the פסח meat next to the oven should, if he is smart, fill his stomach right there. If the group wants to do him a favor, they may come, sit next to him, and eat, according to רבי יהודה. If they want, yes. If they do not want, no. But why? Let him tell them, 'You accepted me!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof for the 'fine hands' question. It uses a משנה where the group can choose not to accommodate one of its members.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the שמש ate a כזית by the oven, that spot becomes his place for eating the פסח, so he cannot eat anywhere else. The משנה says the group joins him only 'if they want.' That means the claim 'you accepted me, so you must accommodate me' does not work, which seems to show the group can also limit a big eater.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: an introduction to a proof from a source
Attendant or waiter serving the group
Olive-size amount, the minimum measure for eating
Smart, sensible
But you accepted me (into the group)

steps.confusionAlert: Why can't the waiter just go back to the table? Because a פסח is eaten in one place. Once he ate a כזית by the oven, that became his eating spot. Moving and eating more elsewhere is a problem.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

If they want, yes; if they don't want, no.

phrases.english: But why?

phrases.notes: Since this claim is not accepted, the group has the upper hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַשַּׁמָּשׁ שֶׁאָכַל כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר בְּצַד הַתַּנּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected in Step 4, a second proof is offered.
steps.raayaObject: That a group may limit a member despite his claim 'you accepted me'
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה about the שמש who ate a כזית by the oven (רבי יהודה)

steps.title: A waiter is different: he was accepted to serve
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The group can tell the waiter they accepted him so he would work for them, not so they would go out of their way for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because they can say to him: 'When we accepted you, it was so that you would work for us. We did not accept you so that we would have to go to trouble for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the waiter proof. A waiter's case is special, so it says nothing about a normal member who eats a lot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The waiter joined the group on the understanding that he would serve them. Asking the whole group to move to the oven reverses that deal. A regular member with 'fine hands' was not accepted as a servant, so this proof fails too. The next step brings a source that settles the question.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there: a standard rejection formula
With the understanding / on condition that
To exert oneself, to go to trouble

phrases.english: It is different there,
because they say to him:
When we accepted you,

For us to exert ourselves for you,
for that we did not accept you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the שמש case; the question itself is settled in step 7.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The waiter was accepted on a special condition (to serve), which does not apply to an ordinary member.

steps.title: A ברייתא openly allows limiting a big eater
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states clearly that a group may tell a member with 'fine hands' to take his share and leave, even at a five-person shared meal. The גמרא concludes: learn from this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if one member of a group has 'fine hands,' they may tell him, 'Take your share and leave.' And not only that, but even five people who made a shared meal may tell him, 'Take your share and leave.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that answers the question directly, and accepts it as the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier proofs, this source talks about exactly our case: a member who grabs a lot. It says the group may limit him to his own portion. The words 'שמע מינה' show that the גמרא treats this as settled.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Fine hands': someone who grabs and eats a lot
They are permitted
Take your share and leave
A shared friendly meal where everyone chips in
Learn from this: the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer to the question: a group may tell a big eater, 'Take your share and leave.' This is true for a פסח and even for an ordinary shared meal.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Members of a group where the hands
of one of them were 'fine' (he ate a lot),
are permitted to say:
'Take your share and leave.'
And not only that, but
even five people who made a shared meal
are permitted to say to him:
'Take your share and leave.'

phrases.notes: The proof is accepted; the question is resolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: בְּנֵי חֲבוּרָה שֶׁהָיָה יָדָיו שֶׁל אֶחָד מֵהֶן יָפוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two failed proofs, a direct source resolves the question.
steps.raayaObject: That a group may limit a member with 'fine hands' to his own share
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about בני חבורה and סיבולת
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A group may tell a big eater, 'Take your share and leave.'

steps.title: What does 'and not only that' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא adds with the phrase 'ולא עוד'. Which case is the bigger חידוש?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'and not only that'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the wording of the ברייתא. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ולא עוד' usually means the second case is a bigger חידוש than the first. The גמרא wants to know why a shared meal would be more surprising than a פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that: introduces a bigger חידוש

phrases.english: What is meant by 'and not only that'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the ruling to the wording of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the shared meal is presented as the greater חידוש

steps.title: Obviously by a פסח, and even by a friendly meal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא speaks in a 'לא מיבעיא' style. By a פסח, it is obvious that the group may limit him, since he was accepted only to help finish the offering. The חידוש is that even at a friendly meal they may limit him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is speaking in the style of 'no need to say.' There is no need to say this about a פסח, where they can tell him, 'We accepted you only to help with the offering.' But even at a shared meal, which is just for friendship, they may tell him, 'Take your share and leave.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. 'ולא עוד' means: the פסח case is obvious, and the shared meal is the bigger חידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a פסח, the group has a strong argument: he was added only so the offering would be fully eaten, not so he could eat more. At a friendly meal, you might think that someone who eats more is welcome for the sake of companionship. Even so, the group may still limit him.

keyTerms.meaning: It is speaking in the style of 'no need to say'
To complete the offering properly, so it is all eaten
Mere companionship

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's order: the פסח case is obvious, because he joined to help finish the offering. The real חידוש is that even at a friendly meal, the group can say, 'Take your share and leave.'

phrases.english: It is speaking in a 'no need to say' style.
There is no need to say this about a פסח,
where they can say to him:
'When we accepted you, it was to help complete the offering,'
but even a shared meal as well,
which is just for companionship,
they are permitted to say to him:
'Take your share and leave.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ולא עוד' is a 'לא מיבעיא' structure: the פסח case is obvious, and the friendly-meal case is the greater חידוש.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A group may limit a big eater both at a פסח and at a friendly shared meal.

steps.title: An alternate version of the question: may a group split up?
steps.stepSummary: Some say the real question was different: may members of a חבורה divide into separate groups, or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: that was not our question. Rather, this is what we asked: are members of a group allowed to split up, or are they not allowed to split up?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a second version of the earlier question. Here the question is whether a group may simply break apart into smaller groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the question was whether the group may push out a member who eats too much. In this version, the question is more general: may the group divide itself even without a special reason? The same sources will now be read with this new question in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say: introduces a second version of the discussion
We asked / it was our question
To divide / split up into separate groups

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand-new topic. It is a different version of the same question from earlier steps, so the same ברייתא will be used to answer it.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
this was not our question,
rather, this is what we asked:
are members of a group permitted to divide up,
or are they not permitted to divide up?

steps.triggerLanguage: איכא דאמרי: הא לא איבעיא לן, אלא הכי הוא דאיבעיא לן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the earlier question with a different version of the same inquiry.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether members of a חבורה may split into separate groups when there is no special reason.

steps.title: The 'fine hands' ברייתא shows they may split only for a reason
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא allows sending away a member with 'fine hands.' This implies that without such a reason, the group may not split. The question is resolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a group in which one member had 'fine hands' (ate a lot) may tell him, 'Take your share and leave.' If his hands are fine, yes. If his hands are not fine, no. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the new question with the same ברייתא as before. It reads it carefully to make an inference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling someone 'take your share and leave' is a kind of splitting the group. The ברייתא allows it only because he eats too much. So without a reason, splitting is not allowed, and the גמרא accepts this with שמע מינה.

keyTerms.meaning: His hands are 'fine': he eats much more and faster than the others
Take your portion and leave
Yes ... no: the גמרא's way of drawing an inference from a condition

steps.whatToRemember: In this version, the הלכה is that a חבורה may split up only when there is a real reason, such as one member eating far more than the others.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
members of a group whose hands,
those of one of them, were fine —
are permitted to say to him:
Take your portion and leave.
If his hands are fine, yes,
phrases.notes: Only with a reason may they split.

phrases.english: if his hands are not fine, no.
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the alternate question from step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That a חבורה may not split up without a reason.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the member with 'fine hands', read through an inference from its condition.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Splitting is allowed only for a reason, such as 'fine hands.'

steps.title: The story: רב פפא eats four slices while רב הונא eats one
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע pooled their bread. רב פפא ate four slices for every one of רב הונא's. רב הונא asked to split the food, and רב פפא replied 'You accepted me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא and רב הונא son of רב יהושע mixed their bread together. While רב הונא ate one piece, רב פפא ate four. רב הונא said: 'Divide it for me.' רב פפא said: 'You accepted me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real story that matches the question exactly. This story sets up the back-and-forth that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא is exactly the 'fine hands' member. רב הונא wants to split off so he gets his fair share. רב פפא argues that by joining the meal, רב הונא agreed to share no matter how much each one eats.

keyTerms.meaning: They mixed (pooled) their bread
Divide for me: split off my share
You accepted (me): you agreed to share with me

phrases.english: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna,
son of Rav Yehoshua,
mixed their bread together with each other.

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּאָכֵיל רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ חֲדָא,
phrases.english: By the time Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua ate one,
Rav Pappa ate four.
He (Rav Huna) said to him: Divide for me.
He (Rav Pappa) said to him: You accepted me.

steps.triggerLanguage: רב פפא ורב הונא בריה דרב יהושע עריבו ריפתא בהדי הדדי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life case of the 'fine hands' question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא claims that agreeing to share a meal prevents the slower eater from splitting off.

steps.title: רב הונא raises all the earlier objections
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא challenges רב פפא with all the sources quoted earlier in the sugya.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רב הונא) raised against him all these objections,
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא attacks רב פפא's claim using the sources from earlier in the sugya, such as the משנה of the שמש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these sources seemed to show that 'you accepted me' cannot force the group to keep sharing. רב הונא uses them to say he may split off.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection against him
Objections / refutations

phrases.english: He raised against him all these objections,

steps.title: רב פפא deflects them as we did
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers each objection the same way the גמרא already answered it.
steps.simpleTranslation: and he (רב פפא) answered as we answered.

steps.deeperAnalysis: For example, with the שמש case, the group accepted him so that he would serve them, not so they would go out of their way for him. So none of these sources proves that a friend at a meal may split off.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier sources show that a group may separate from a member.

steps.title: רב הונא cites the 'fine hands' ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא challenges רב פפא with the ברייתא of בני חבורה, which allows sending away a member with 'fine hands.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised against him the ruling of 'members of a group.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא now quotes the ברייתא that directly allows sending away the big eater. This seems to describe רב פפא exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the source seems to fit the case perfectly: a member with 'fine hands' may be told to take his share and leave. רב פפא must explain why it does not apply to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Members of a group (here, the ברייתא that begins with these words)

phrases.english: He raised against him: 'Members of a group.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A stronger objection after the earlier ones were deflected.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly permits sending away a member with 'fine hands.'

steps.title: רב פפא: that was about the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the ברייתא speaks of a פסח group. There, the member was accepted only to help finish the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, they can say to him, 'When we accepted you, it was to properly handle the offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא limits the ברייתא to a group eating a קרבן פסח, which is different from a friendly meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a פסח group, members join so the offering will be fully eaten, so the group can limit someone who takes too much. At a friendly meal, people join to eat together no matter who eats more. רב פפא uses the same תיקוני זביחה reasoning as step 9, but he stops at the פסח and ignores the ברייתא's next clause about a סיבולת. The next objection exploits exactly that gap.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in that case)
We accepted you
To properly take care of the offering

phrases.english: He said to him: There,
they can say to him: when we accepted you —
it was for the proper handling of the offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה: התם דאמרי ליה כי קבלינך
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the source to a different case (פסח, not a friendly meal).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lets any group send away a big eater.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a פסח group, which formed for the sake of the offering, may do so.

steps.title: רב הונא cites the shared-meal clause
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes the next part of the ברייתא, about a סיבולת (a shared friendly meal).
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised against him the case of a shared meal,
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא brings the 'ולא עוד' clause of the same ברייתא. It allows splitting even at a friendly shared meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's answer covered only the פסח. But the ברייתא goes further and says that even at a regular shared meal, the big eater may be told to take his share. This blocks רב פפא's distinction.

keyTerms.meaning: A shared meal where friends pool their food

phrases.english: He raised against him the shared meal,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defeats the פסח distinction of step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's distinction between a פסח group and a friendly meal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly extends the rule to a friendly shared meal.

steps.title: רב פפא agrees and divides the food
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא accepts the proof and splits the food with רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He divided it for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא has no answer, so he gives in and splits the food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיבולת clause settles the matter. Even at a friendly meal, the slower eater may separate from someone who eats much more than he does.

keyTerms.meaning: He divided for him

steps.whatToRemember: Even at a friendly shared meal, if one person eats far more than the others, the others may split off and take their fair share. This is exactly what the 'ולא עוד' clause of the ברייתא teaches.
steps.whyThisMatters: The story shows the ברייתא's rule being applied in real life, and it confirms that the חידוש from step 9 (it applies even at a friendly meal) is the הלכה.

phrases.english: He divided for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב פפא accepts the objection of step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: At a shared meal, a member may split off from a much bigger eater; 'you accepted me' does not stop him.

steps.title: Eating together with רבינא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע shared a meal with רבינא, who ate eight pieces for every one of his. He joked that a hundred רב פפא's are better than one רבינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and shared his food with רבינא. By the time רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע ate one piece, רבינא ate eight. He said: 'Better a hundred פפא's than one רבינא!'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues with a funny ending. רב הונא now shares a meal with רבינא and finds that רבינא eats far more than רב פפא did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier story, רב הונא wanted to split from רב פפא because רב פפא ate a lot. Now he sees that רבינא eats much more, so he jokes that רב פפא was a much better meal partner. This closes the story, which illustrated the rule that even at a סיבולת (shared friendly meal) one may split off from a much bigger eater.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixed / combined (his food with someone else's)
Together with
Eight
A hundred people like רב פפא

phrases.english: He went and mixed his food together with Ravina.

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּאָכֵיל רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ חֲדָא,
phrases.english: By the time Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua ate one piece,
Ravina ate eight.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: מְאָה פָּפֵּי וְלָא חֲדָא רָבִינָא.
phrases.english: He said: a hundred Pappas, and not one Ravina!
phrases.notes: A joke. It is better to eat with a hundred people like רב פפא than with one רבינא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story about רב פפא and רב הונא with a lighthearted ending.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No new הלכה. This is a humorous end to the story.

steps.title: A ברייתא on money for a share in a פסח versus selling an עולה or שלמים
steps.stepSummary: Money taken for a share in a פסח or חגיגה is חולין. Selling an עולה or שלמים does nothing, and the money goes to נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: if someone signs others up with him on his פסח or his חגיגה, the money he received is חולין (not holy). But if someone sells his עולה or his שלמים, he has done nothing, and whatever money he received goes to נדבה (communal free-will offerings).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that compares two cases of taking money for a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Joining others onto your פסח or חגיגה is allowed, so the money you get from them becomes ordinary חולין money. Selling an עולה or שלמים does not work at all, because a קרבן belongs to גבוה, not to its owner. Still, the money does not go back to the buyer. It must be used for נדבה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who registers others as partners in a קרבן
His חגיגה, the festival peace-offering of י״ד ניסן
Non-sacred, ordinary
His burnt-offering and peace-offerings
To the fund for communal free-will offerings

steps.confusionAlert: Both cases involve taking money for a קרבן, but the results are opposite. In the פסח case the money is free to use. In the selling case the money is taken away for נדבה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who registers others with him
on his Paschal lamb and on his festival offering —
the money in his hand is non-sacred.
And one who sells his burnt-offering and his peace-offerings —
has done nothing at all,
and the money, whatever amount it is, goes to free-will offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: taking money in exchange for a share in a קרבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money for a share in a פסח or חגיגה is חולין. Selling an עולה or שלמים is void, and the money goes to נדבה.

steps.title: If the sale did nothing, why is the money taken?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the money must go to נדבה if the sale is completely void.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since he did nothing, why should the money go to נדבה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second half of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sale is void, the money never became holy and should simply be returned to the buyer. So why does the ברייתא send it to נדבה?

keyTerms.meaning: Since
Why?

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּלֹא עָשָׂה וְלֹא כְּלוּם,
phrases.english: But since he did nothing at all,
why should the money go to free-will offerings?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּלֹא עָשָׂה וְלֹא כְּלוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's ruling about the money.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A void sale should leave the money as the buyer's ordinary money. Nothing should send it to נדבה.

steps.title: It is a penalty
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the Rabbis imposed a קנס (penalty).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it is a penalty.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. The money goes to נדבה as a punishment from the Rabbis, not because the sale worked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under תורה law the money is not holy. The Rabbis penalized the people involved so that no one would try to buy and sell קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: A penalty/fine (from the Rabbis)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a rabbinic penalty can explain a result that the basic law alone would not produce.

phrases.english: Rava said: it is a penalty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The money should go back because the sale was void.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sale is void under תורה law, but the Rabbis fined the people involved.

steps.title: What does 'whatever amount' add?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks what the extra words 'כל שהן' come to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the meaning of 'כל שהן' (whatever amount)?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is setting up the next move. He asks what the extra words in the ברייתא add.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא could have just said 'the money goes to נדבה.' The added 'כל שהן' must be teaching something more.

keyTerms.meaning: Whatever amount they are

phrases.english: And what is 'whatever amount'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reason for the קנס to the exact wording of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra case the words 'כל שהן' include.

steps.title: Even the overpayment is penalized
steps.stepSummary: If the animal was worth four and the buyer paid five, even the extra one goes to נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if the animals were worth only four and they gave him five, the Rabbis fined him even on that extra amount.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers that 'כל שהן' includes overpayment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the extra money was a gift, separate from the price of the קרבן, and so the seller could keep it. 'כל שהן' teaches that the penalty covers every coin he received.

keyTerms.meaning: Four (זוז)
Five (זוז)
The extra amount
They penalized him

steps.whatToRemember: Selling a קרבן is void. The Rabbis still take all the money received, even an overpayment, as a קנס for נדבה.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הֲווֹ שָׁווּ אֶלָּא אַרְבְּעָה,
phrases.english: even though they were worth only four,
and they gave him five —
even regarding that extra amount
the Rabbis also penalized him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הֲווֹ שָׁווּ אֶלָּא אַרְבְּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כל שהן' includes overpayment beyond the animal's value. That extra money is also penalized.

steps.title: How can holiness move onto something already holy?
steps.stepSummary: עולא asks about the first ruling. The lamb is already הקדש for a פסח, so how can the קדושה of the joining member's money move onto it and make the money חולין?
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said (and some say רבי אושעיא): Do our Babylonian friends perhaps know the reason for this? This man set aside a lamb for his פסח, and that man set aside money for his פסח. How can הקדש take effect on something that is already הקדש? Yet the ברייתא teaches that the money in his hand is חולין!
steps.whatsHappening: עולא returns to the first half of the ברייתא and raises a puzzle. He opens with a teasing challenge to the Babylonian scholars to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new member's money was set aside for his פסח, so it is holy. It can only become חולין if its קדושה moves onto the lamb. But the lamb is already fully holy as a פסח, and normally הקדש cannot take effect on something that is already הקדש. So how does the money become חולין?

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another name for the speaker)
Our Babylonian colleagues
Set aside / designated
A lamb
Holiness taking effect on something already holy

steps.confusionAlert: עולא is not asking whether one may sign people onto a פסח, since that is clearly allowed. He is asking how the money's holiness gets transferred so that the money ends up as חולין.

phrases.english: Ulla said, and some say it was Rabbi Oshaya:
Is it possible that our Babylonian colleagues know
the reason for this matter?
This one set aside a lamb for his Paschal offering,
and this one set aside money for his Paschal offering —
how does consecration take effect on something already consecrated,
since it teaches: the money in his hand is non-sacred?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: אֶפְשָׁר יָדְעִי חַבְרִין בַּבְלָאֵי טַעְמָא דְּהַאי מִלְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first clause of the ברייתא from step 20 and questions how it works.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling 'מעות שבידו חולין' in the case of joining others onto a פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The money can only lose its קדושה by moving it onto the lamb. But the lamb is already הקדש, and הקדש cannot take effect on הקדש.
